title: Intermediate Backend Engineer - Code Security
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI) as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

Intermediate Backend Engineer, Security Factory: Code Security

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in the code they write and the open source components they depend on.

Your work connects dependency analysis, vulnerability detection, and automated remediation. You'll build parsing that tells the security analysis engine which libraries and frameworks a project uses, extend a service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, and develop hybrid analyzers that combine rule-based detection with artificial intelligence (AI) reasoning. You'll help evaluate how well those analyzers find real vulnerabilities and expand coverage of libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling.

We use AI-assisted development tools in our daily work and expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.

What you’ll do

• Develop secure, well-tested, performant parsing for dependency manifests, lockfiles, and software bills of materials (SBOMs). Extend support for new package ecosystems and formats in the analysis engine and remediation service.

• Build and apply analyzers that combine deterministic analysis with AI-driven analysis, working with the team's technical leadership. Review their results and measure false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.

• Create detection rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the test fixtures that prove they work.

• Contribute to packaging analyzers for continuous integration (CI) jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, reporting findings in GitLab's standard security report formats.

• Extend the automated remediation service, from running dependency updates in a sandbox to opening merge requests.

• Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity. Identify technical debt that slows the team down, and propose and implement improvements.

• Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.

• Participate in on-call rotations to troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.

What you’ll bring

• Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't.

• Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust. We use both, plus Ruby for remediation and Python for some analyzers, and value a willingness to work across them.

• A willingness to learn how vulnerabilities arise in code and the software supply chain, explore common vulnerability classes such as the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP) Top 10 and CWE, and apply static analysis to detect them. Deep expertise isn't required, and we'll help you develop it.

• The ability to organize your work and follow through on tasks independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.

• The ability to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems and propose iterative solutions.

• Helpful, but not required: experience with containerized workflows and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), or a willingness to learn them; package managers and dependency tooling such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo; web or mobile frameworks; parsing, abstract syntax trees (ASTs), program analysis, or detection rules; or evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data. We use Docker heavily.

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing (SAST) and dependency scanning.

We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

• Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being (https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/)

• Flexible Paid Time Off  (https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto)

• Team Member Resource Groups (https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/)

• Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan (https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/)

• Growth and Development Fund (https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/)

• Parental Leave (https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave)

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups (https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups) are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. (https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/) Your privacy is important to us.

GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy (https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#equal-employment-opportunity-policy) and EEO is the Law (https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/labor-and-employment-notices/#eeoc-us-equal-employment-opportunity-commission-notices). If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation (https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#reasonable-accommodation), please let us know during the recruiting process (https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/interviewing/#adjustments-to-our-interview-process).

title: Site Reliability Engineer, Cells Infrastructure
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI) as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

We're looking for an Intermediate Site Reliability Engineer to join the Cells Infrastructure team in GitLab's Scale & Architecture organization. In this role, you'll help build and operate Cells, the architecture that lets GitLab.com scale horizontally. Cells splits GitLab.com into many independent units, each with its own application and data stack, behind a shared routing layer.

This is a build-it-and-run-it role. You'll provision cells, route traffic to them, deploy them safely, and keep them reliable in production. You'll also help move customer organizations onto Cells, one of GitLab's most important scaling initiatives.

What you'll do

• Operate Cells in production: join the on-call rotation, respond to incidents, lead post-incident reviews, and drive corrective actions to completion.

• Define and monitor service level objectives (SLOs) for routing and cell health, and build the dashboards, alerts, and runbooks behind them.

• Provision and operate cell infrastructure on Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including Kubernetes, networking, Identity and Access Management (IAM), PostgreSQL, Redis, and object storage.

• Develop infrastructure as code with Terraform, Helm, and GitOps tooling such as Argo CD.

• Operate and extend the global routing layer, built on Cloudflare Workers, Envoy, and a Go service backed by Cloud Spanner, and expand routing to more protocols and services.

• Improve the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines behind ring-based deployments, covering promotion, database migrations, quality assurance validation, and rollback.

• Support organization migrations by preparing destination cells and helping with dry runs and production cutovers.

• Work with product teams to make their services cell-compatible, and write documentation so others can operate Cells with confidence.

What you'll bring

• Professional experience running production infrastructure at scale on AWS, GCP, or both, including Kubernetes, along with strong Terraform and Helm skills.

• Proficiency in Go, or strong experience in another systems language and willingness to work in Go daily.

• Solid grounding in site reliability engineering (SRE) best practices: SLOs and error budgets, blameless post-incident reviews, reducing toil through automation, capacity planning, and designing for graceful degradation.

• Experience owning services in production, including on-call, incident response, and monitoring with tools such as Prometheus and Grafana.

• Practical knowledge of progressive delivery: how to roll changes safely across a fleet and how to roll them back.

• A strong understanding of distributed-systems fundamentals, such as request routing, proxies, consistency, and failure domains.

• Experience working effectively in distributed, all-remote teams: you default to asynchronous, written-first communication, document decisions in issues and merge requests, hand off work cleanly across time zones, and stay transparent about progress and blockers.

Every team in our organization owns its services end to end, from design through on-call.We own the control plane that tracks cells and decides where each request belongs, and keep the fleet in step with GitLab's release cadence.We work closely with delivery, database, migration, and product teams across GitLab. title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks (Contract)
description:
Headquarters: Australia

URL: https://www.askablelabs.com/

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works

• Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.

• Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.

• Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.

• Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.

• Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.

• Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.

• Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

Requirements

• 2+ years of professional software engineering

• Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)

• Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++

• Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing

• Regular use of an AI coding tool

• Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models

• You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words

• At least 10 hours a week, starting now

• A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

Nice to have

• Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure

• Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

Terms

• US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you

• Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms

• The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

• Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/askable-software-engineer-ai-coding-tasks-contract

title: Staff Software Engineer (SRE)
description:
Phantom (https://phantom.com) is on a mission to connect the world to the freedom of open markets. Tens of millions of people all over the world use Phantom (https://jobicy.com/company/phantom) to access global markets that never close, including perpetuals, prediction markets, tokenized assets, stablecoins and memes. Phantom users are able to discover the markets that matter and the cultural moments that shape them, building conviction through real-time data and the verified performance of top traders. With self-custody and access to open networks at its core, Phantom lets them control their financial moves in the same app they use to safely store or spend money worldwide.

Phantom has reached #1 in Google Play's finance category and consistently ranks in the top 50 apps across all categories. Check out ourForbes Fintech 50 (https://www.forbes.com/sites/ninabambysheva/2026/02/23/inside-phantoms-battle-plan-to-win-the-crypto-fueled-superapp-war/) and CNBC and Statista'sWorld's Top Fintech Companies 2026 (https://www.cnbc.com/worlds-top-fintech-companies-2026/)!

We are around 180 people, fully remote, backed by a $150M Series C investment from a16z, Sequoia Capital and Paradigm.

Responsibilities

•
Kubernetes Ownership: Manage and scale Kubernetes clusters on AWS EKS, ensuring reliability, performance, and security.

•
Infrastructure Automation: Implement and maintain Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform/Pulumi) to automate infrastructure provisioning and management.

•
Performance Optimization: Monitor and optimize system performance, scalability, and resource utilization.

•
Blockchain Infrastructure: Configure and maintain crypto nodes across multiple blockchains to support our wallet’s operations.

•
Database Scaling: Optimize and scale database infrastructure to handle terabytes of blockchain data efficiently.

•
System Reliability: Continuously improve system uptime, monitoring, and observability using tools like Datadog and OpenTelemetry.

•
Collaboration: Work closely with backend and product teams to support feature development and system scaling.

Qualifications

•
5+ years in a SRE or Software Engineer role.

•
Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes (EKS) in production environments.

•
Proficiency with AWS infrastructure and services (EC2, S3, RDS, IAM).

•
Solid experience with Docker and Infrastructure-as-Code tools like Terraform or Pulumi.

•
Monitoring and observability experience using tools like Datadog or OpenTelemetry.

The target base salary for this role will range between $200,000 to $250,000 with the addition of equity and benefits. This is determined by a few factors including your skillset, prior relevant experience, quality of interviews and market factors (such as location) at the point in time of offer.

Why Work With Us

Phantom's journey to becoming a global trading app began with making crypto easier to use. Today, we’re building on that foundation to help people discover the markets that matter, make informed financial moves, and safely store or spend their money worldwide. Joining Phantom means helping shape that next chapter: building products that bring the freedom of open markets to more people.

•
Build for global impact: Create products used by tens of millions of people, making innovative financial markets more accessible to users around the world.

•
Make complexity feel simple: Solve meaningful challenges across design, engineering, and user experience to make discovering markets and managing money seamless.

•
Put users in control: Help build a future where people have greater freedom over their assets and financial decisions, with security and self-custody at the foundation.

Benefits (only available to full-time employees)

•
Competitive salary and equity

•
Comprehensive insurance (medical/dental/vision): base plan 100% covered

•
Flexible hours and a long-standing, supportive remote environment

•
Unlimited vacation: Take time when you need it (and we really mean it!)

•
401(k) retirement plan

•
Wellness stipend

•
Weekly meal stipend

•
Learning & Development stipend

•
Remote / WFH set-up stipend

We strongly encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We believe that our work is stronger with a variety of perspectives, and we’re eager to further diversify our company. If you have a background that you feel would make an impact at Phantom, please consider applying. We’re committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best work of your career.

By submitting your resume and application materials, you acknowledge and agree that Phantom Technologies, Inc. ("Phantom") collects and processes your personal information (including application materials, interview records, and related data) to evaluate your candidacy. Phantom may use AI-powered tools and third-party service providers for transcription, note-taking, scheduling, and other administrative tasks. Phantom does not sell your information and your materials will be handled securely and in accordance with applicable data protection laws.

An overview of this role

As an Threat Research Engineer at GitLab, you'll research emerging security threats and turn your findings into protection for GitLab customers. You'll investigate new attack surfaces, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems, and build systems that help detect threats and improve vulnerability advisories.
This is a full-stack role: you'll take an idea from the first research question to a working proof of concept, deploy it, and analyze the results yourself. Artificial intelligence (AI) is central to how we work. You'll use AI tools daily and build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection.

What you'll do

• Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems.

• Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools.

• Analyze software supply chain incidents and events.

• Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection.

• Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work.

• Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories.

• Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences.

What you'll bring

• Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with an understanding of package ecosystems and software supply chain attacks.

• Both a developer mindset and an adversarial mindset: you can build systems and think about how to break them.

• Demonstrated experience using AI in real work, such as building with large language model (LLM) application programming interfaces (APIs) or agent frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or agent software development kits (SDKs).

• Strong programming skills in Go or Python, with good software engineering practices, including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and writing maintainable code.

• Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud.

• The ability to map attack vectors, explain trade-offs, and use data to move experiments forward, balancing quality, speed, and customer outcomes.

• Clear writing for engineers and a general audience, and keeping up with security and AI industry trends.

• Helpful, but not required: Google Cloud Platform (GCP); Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entries or published findings; research on AI agents, LLM applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; blogs, talks, or open source security tools; Terraform or OpenTofu; databases or data pipelines at scale; reverse engineering.

• You don't need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing (SAST) engines. A high-level understanding is enough.

About the team
We're the Threat Research group. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database, which powers GitLab's dependency scanning, and publish our findings on the Security Labs blog.
Our work includes research on the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Serena, a popular MCP coding agent.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

An overview of this role

Help us build the next generation of authentication services at GitLab. As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Authentication team, you'll build authentication features across the Rails monolith and GATE. GATE is our new service for issuing and validating tokens and managing identities, designed to support every GitLab deployment model.

You'll expand authentication mechanisms, including support for identities used by artificial intelligence (AI) agents. You'll also help keep GitLab and its customers secure by building access management tooling and addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.

GATE will become the foundation for token issuance, validation, and identity services across GitLab.com multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS), Self-Managed, Dedicated, and air-gapped environments. Your work will affect core components that customers, users, and GitLab teams rely on.

Some of our projects include:

• Building GATE as the centralized service for token issuance and validation

• Consolidating tokens and migrating authentication paths out of the Rails monolith

• Building passkeys and passwordless authentication

• Developing composite identities that combine machine and human authorization for AI

• Improving service accounts and secure automation

• Enhancing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), OpenID Connect (OIDC), and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) capabilities for automated user provisioning and single sign-on (SSO)

What you'll do

• Shape the roadmap for GATE and GitLab's authentication services with the team.

• Design and implement token issuance, validation, and identity services in Go and Ruby across the Rails monolith and GATE, including new authentication mechanisms such as Workload Identity Federation.

• Migrate authentication and token management paths from the monolith into GATE while maintaining reliability across all deployment models.

• Build authentication mechanisms from the ground up, such as Workload Identity Federation.

• Strengthen security for users and organizations through access management tooling and by addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.

• Define and improve standards for style, maintainability, and engineering practices in a high-scale environment, and advocate for them through code review.

• Communicate publicly about GitLab initiatives, projects, and contributions from people not working for GitLab Inc. Reflect GitLab's values in these communications.

• Ship moderately sized features and improvements with moderate guidance and support from other team members, and collaborate on larger projects, including the build-out of GATE.

• Participate in the maintainer trainee program at your own comfortable pace while working toward becoming a project maintainer.

What you'll bring

• Professional experience with Go and/or Ruby in scaling or mission-critical SaaS products.

• Familiarity with authentication and authorization technologies or techniques, such as OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SSO, SCIM, LDAP, JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), role-based access control (RBAC), or identity and access management (IAM).

• Knowledge of token systems, cryptographic signing, and key management.

• Experience building or contributing to a service from concept to production, including proposal, discussion, and execution.

• Proficiency in written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate complex problems and solutions clearly in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.

• Experience diagnosing, preventing, and resolving performance and optimization problems.

• Experience working in an iterative software development process, managing your work effectively, staying organized, and following through on priorities.

About the team

Our mission is to empower GitLab system administrators with the toolkit they need to create their desired balance of security and accessibility for their GitLab experience.

Authentication is the first impression a new customer has when they configure a new GitLab instance. We aim to make it as seamless as possible, from that first login to onboarding users and managing security rules for their instance in a secure, flexible, and scalable way.

title: Software Engineer - Auth
description:
About Supabase (https://jobicy.com/company/supabase)

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the role

Auth (https://supabase.com/auth), written in Go (https://github.com/supabase/auth) (server) and with client libraries for TypeScript (https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js), SSR (https://github.com/supabase/ssr) and for other frameworks and technologies, is one of the most popular products in the Supabase stack. We are seeking someone to help us build new and maintain existing Auth features.

What you’ll be responsible for

•
Designing and implementing secure, scalable authentication features in Go and TypeScript.

•
Working across the stack: from server-side protocols to client-side libraries for frameworks like Next.js.

•
Owning the performance, reliability, and scalability of the Auth server across Supabase's infrastructure.

•
Contributing to the evolution of our Auth architecture, including support for OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and other protocols.

•
Planning and executing safe database migrations across a large fleet of Postgres instances.

•
Building and improving observability: metrics, tracing, alerting, and dashboards to keep the system healthy at scale.

•
Writing and reviewing RFCs as part of our product development process.

•
Collaborating with engineers across Supabase to ensure a seamless experience for developers using our tools.

•
Supporting the community and responding to developer feedback on GitHub, Discord, and other channels.

You might be a good fit if you

•
(Required) Have 4+ years of professional experience writing and shipping Go in production.

•
(Required) Have 2+ years of professional experience working on an authentication system (implementing protocol support, maintenance at scale).

•
(Required) Have strong relational database experience (Postgres or MySQL); Postgres experience is a bonus.

•
Have strong knowledge of TypeScript in addition to Go (languages used daily).

•
Have strong knowledge of web technology fundamentals (cookies, sessions, JWT, HTTP, browser APIs).

•
Have good knowledge of and deep interest in authentication security (passwords, protocols such as OAuth, OIDC or SAML, cryptography fundamentals such as hash functions, signatures and ciphers).

•
Have experience working with multiple web frameworks like Next.js (or other SSR alternative in the JavaScript space) and traditional web frameworks like Ruby on Rails, Django, Laravel or equivalent (in any language).

•
Have good technical writing skills (RFC process is an important part of making changes to the Auth product).

•
Have hands-on experience building and operating services at significant scale.

•
Have deep understanding of systems-level concerns: memory management, concurrency patterns, and compute resource optimization in Go.

•
Have experience with Kubernetes and AWS (or comparable cloud platform) in a production setting.

•
Have solid grasp of observability practices — metrics, distributed tracing, structured logging, and alerting (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry).

•
Have experience managing database schema migrations safely at scale.

What We Offer

•
Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•
ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•
Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•
Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•
Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•
Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•
Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•
~400 team members

•
60+ countries

•
20+ languages spoken

•
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Postgres Deployment Engineer (Nix)
description:
About Supabase (https://jobicy.com/company/supabase)

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Postgres Deployment Engineer to join our PostgreSQL team and help elevate our PostgreSQL offerings.

You’ll work closely with the PostgreSQL team, playing an instrumental role in technical decision-making and refining internal methodologies. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

The focus of this role is owning the stability and deployment of our products. You will act as a bridge between product and infrastructure teams to improve the reliability of deployments and upgrades. You will have co-responsibility for builds and deployments via our public supabase/postgres GitHub repository, which bundles features into Docker images and AWS AMIs for cloud and local use.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

•
Package software into our supabase/postgres repo using Nix (with flakes), and help us transition our packaging from traditional to Nix packaging more over time.

•
Manage PostgreSQL lifecycles, ensuring timely major, minor, and extension upgrades.

•
Expand platform release systems to allow developers to increasingly self-service.

•
Optimize CI/CD and tooling, specifically expanding GitHub Actions, team tooling, and testing/release approaches.

•
Resolve production issues by proactively identifying and fixing problems in customer deployments.

•
Maintain best practices and tests to ensure enhanced stability and decreased deployment risks.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

•
Have 3+ years of experience with PostgreSQL and its ecosystem, including extensions and performance optimization.

•
Are an Infrastructure Expert with proven experience in management, tooling, and optimization.

•
Are proficient in the Nix package management system (including flakes) alongside Ansible, Packer, Docker, QEMU/KVM, AWS, and Kubernetes.

•
Have experience building for multiple architectures, specifically Linux and Darwin/macOS aarch64 targets.

•
Are comfortable with polyglot environments, including builds for C/C++, Go, JavaScript, and Rust-based projects.

•
Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences, especially when interacting with customers.

•
Have experience in async or globally distributed teams and value independent, proactive problem-solving.

•
Are willing to mentor, taking on responsibility for teaching the engineering team to use and contribute to our Nix-based work.

What We Offer

•
Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•
ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•
Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•
Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•
Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•
Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•
Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•
~400 team members

•
60+ countries

•
20+ languages spoken

•
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: AI Experience Engineer (Conversational AI)
description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote)

About the Role:

An AI Experience Engineer owns the full lifecycle of the journeys our customers have with Upgrade's AI agent on chat, voice and email: creation, optimization, edge case handling and containment growth. They build journeys in Sierra's no-code tooling, partner with Upgrade's product groups to bring their servicing flows to the agent, and are accountable for whether the agent resolves the customer's issue safely, accurately and without a human.

We are hiring an AI Experience Engineer to own Upgrade's customer-facing AI agent. You will sit between engineering, product and customer operations. You will turn servicing workflows, such as making a payment, checking loan details, updating an address or enabling autopay, into production journeys and keep improving them after launch. You will build and own the journeys end to end, from first draft to steady state. The work is part builder, part analyst: design the flow, handle the edge cases, read the transcripts, and keep raising containment. Containment, CSAT, transfer quality and hallucination rate are your metrics.

Within your first year, you will own a portfolio of journeys across products (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, HELOC, Deposits) and help set the standards for how Upgrade builds, tests and ships AI experiences.

Our Core Technologies

Sierra Agent Studio (no-code journeys), Sierra simulations and conversation analytics, GraphQL and REST APIs (as journey tools), Genesys (contact center handoff), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, Javascript/Typescript, Claude and other LLM tools.

What You'll Do

• Journey creation: Design and build Sierra journeys in Agent Studio for chat, voice and email, from discovery with operations through production rollout

• Optimization: Review transcripts, recordings and analytics every week, find where conversations fail or transfer, and ship fixes to journey logic, instructions and knowledge

• Edge case handling: Map the unhappy paths (failed payments, mismatched identity, delinquent accounts, unsupported requests) and make sure each ends in a correct answer or a clean handoff

• Containment: Own containment and CSAT targets per journey, run staged rollouts (1% → 100%), and prioritize the work that moves those numbers most

• Product partnership: Work with product groups (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, Deposits) to scope new journeys, keep journeys current as products change, and define the APIs the agent needs

• Safety and compliance: Apply tiered authentication and step-up verification, verbatim compliance language and guardrails against hallucination and off-policy answers

• Handoffs: Design transfers to human agents in Genesys with accurate summaries and auth context

• Testing: Build simulation and regression suites so every journey change ships with evidence it did not break existing behavior

• Monitoring: Watch latency, errors and drop-offs in SumoLogic and Grafana, and own the alerts

• Voice tuning: Latency, filler phrases, interruptions, personality and tone

• Sierra relationship: Be the technical owner on our side, escalate platform issues and shape roadmap asks

What We Look For:

• 3–5 years of Frontend Software Engineering experience, or equivalent experience in Solutions Engineering, Conversational AI or Technical Product roles

• Working knowledge of how LLM agents behave: instructions, tool calls, knowledge retrieval, and where each one fails

• Experience building evaluations for non-deterministic systems: test sets, simulations, LLM-as-judge, regression gates

• Enough technical depth to read API specs, work with backend engineers on REST and GraphQL integrations, and reason about authorization and permission scopes

• Working knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to build and maintain coded journeys and integrate APIs within conversational AI platforms.

• Product and customer mindset: you understand ops procedures, you read transcripts, care about tone, and measure success by whether the customer's problem got solved

• Ownership in production: rollouts, monitoring, log analysis and incident response

• Clear writing and the ability to work with non-engineers in operations, compliance and legal

Nice To Have:

• Hands-on experience with Sierra Agent Studio, or a comparable no-code agent platform (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect)

• Voice AI experience: speech-to-text, text-to-speech, latency tuning, barge-in handling

• Contact center systems such as Genesys, and agent handoff design

• Background in fintech or another regulated industry (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2)

• Conversation design or UX writing experience

What We Offer You:

• Competitive salary ($140K-$180K CAN) and stock option plan

• Paid coverage of medical, dental and vision insurance

• Flexible PTO

• Opportunities for professional growth and development
• Paid parental leave

• Health & wellness initiatives

tone, and measure success by whether the customer's problem got solved • Ownership in production: rollouts, monitoring, log analysis and incident response • Clear writing and the ability to work with Lex/Connect) • Voice AI experience: speech-to-text, text-to-speech, latency tuning, barge-in handling • Contact center systems such as Genesys, and agent handoff design • Background in fintech or title: Monetization Operations Analyst
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Finance Operations (FinOps) team provides and enhances core business services that are the backbone of Stripe. FinOps uses data and operational excellence to deliver technology solutions, payroll services, operational excellence, and monetization services to Stripe.

What you'll do

We're looking for a Monetization Operations Analyst to join our growing team. You'll help us improve user experience through accurate and timely onboarding of contracts and workflows, and deliver improvements in our integrated financial systems with business partners, financial colleagues, and engineers.

Responsibilities

• Onboard sold custom contracts into our billing systems.

• Work with legal contracts with strong attention to detail and accuracy.

• Develop and manage scalable billing and collection processes for complex user agreements and new business operations.

• Build scalable and auditable onboarding processes for new and existing users.

• Partner with internal systems, global deal management, legal, sales ops, internal audit, go-to-market, engineering, and accounting teams to develop and improve processes for contract reviews and to anticipate changing business requirements.

• Partner with account managers to resolve user inquiries related to onboarding implementation, billing, and collections.

• Advocate for the customer to internal stakeholders. Share system feedback and insights with Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Support, and Legal on innovation and improvements needed to optimize the Stripe user experience.

• Help scope, build, and deliver continuous process improvements that enhance operations.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 5+ years of experience in a client-facing role, ideally in customer success, consulting, financial services, account management, or sales, preferably working with technical products.

• Track record of leading technical conversations and persuading others to take action based on requirements and value provided by solutions.

• Ability to be detail-oriented while visualizing the larger impact of a series of transactions.

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to navigate data and people to find answers.

• Strong operating rigor, including organizational and time management skills.

• Ability to work well with a wide range of people, both internally and externally, including working with a team of sales and services peers.

• Motivation and flexibility to work well in a high-growth environment where things change quickly.

Preferred qualifications

• Ability to trace process impacts from situation to end customers and business financial outcomes.

• Knowledge of or experience in the payments industry.

• Demonstrated professional experience using GSuite, Excel, and working with large data sets.

• Experience with SQL.

• Demonstrated project management or consulting experience and the ability to work cross-functionally.

• A builder's mindset and a willingness to question assumptions and conventional wisdom.

• A passion for learning and solving problems through infrastructure and automation.

title: Corporate Accounting Analyst (Bangalore)
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

To further this important mission, we're building our Accounting team in Bangalore Finance and are looking for someone to help us scale for the future in a fast-paced environment.

Role Summary

We are seeking a highly detail-oriented and tech-forward Corporate Accounting Analyst to join our fast-paced corporate accounting team. In this role, you will play a critical part in managing General Ledger (GL) activities, ensuring accurate close processes, and driving accounting precision across specialized technical areas, including debt, prepaids, intercompany transactions, and lease accounting .

The ideal candidate holds a Chartered Accountant (CA) qualification, possesses 4–6 years of progressive accounting experience, and brings a modern, tech-enabled mindset—specifically the ability to leverage AI tools, automation, and advanced analytics to streamline workflows and solve complex accounting problems in a rapidly evolving environment.

Key Responsibilities

• Own end-to-end accounting schedules, journal entries, and balance sheet reconciliations for corporate accounting areas .

• Manage month-end, quarter-end, and year-end closing activities within prescribed timelines.

• Conduct variance analyses on P&L and Balance Sheet line items, investigating unexpected fluctuations and providing actionable commentary to management.

• Support internal and external audit requests by preparing audit schedules, supporting documentation, and clear accounting workpapers.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams (F&S, FinOps, Tax, Operations) to ensure accurate accounting treatment for complex transactions.

• Leverage ERP automation, analytical capabilities and AI-driven tools (e.g., prompt engineering, automated reconciliation workflows, intelligent data extraction) to enhance accuracy and timeliness.

• Identify bottlenecks in the financial close cycle and implement automated solutions or streamlined workflows.

• Utilize advanced data tools to process large volumes of financial data accurately under tight deadliness.

Required Qualifications & Experience

• Education & Certification: Chartered Accountant (CA) or equivalent professional accounting designation is mandatory.

• Experience: 4 to 6 years of post-qualification core corporate accounting experience, with strong hands-on expertise in General Ledger operations.

• AI & Tech Proficiency: Demonstrated ability to adopt and operate AI tools (e.g., generative AI for documentation/analysis, workflow automation software, advanced ERP modules) to optimize accounting tasks.

Key Competencies & Soft Skills

• Fast-Paced Adaptability: Ability to prioritize effectively, meet tight monthly/quarterly closing deadlines, and thrive in an agile, dynamic environment.

• Analytical & Detail-Oriented: Exceptional problem-solving skills with a high degree of precision in numerical and technical accounting work.

• Communication: Clear verbal and written communication skills to effectively collaborate with remote teams, management, and external auditors.

• Self-Starter: Strong ownership mindset, able to work independently as a contractor with minimal supervision.

Nice to Have

• Knowledge of (or experience in) the technology or payments industry

• Big4 working experience

• Oracle suite

• Hubble and SQL

title: Head of Technology
description:
Headquarters: New York City

URL: https://sanctuary.computer

We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.

Original job posting link (https://garden3d.notion.site/Head-of-Technology-3f9131fea2c7815da5e3ec914835c397?source=copy_link)

About garden3d (https://garden3d.net/)

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development

At Sanctuary Computer (https://www.sanctuary.computer/) we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design

When we started XXIX (https://www.xxix.co/) in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Index - Community

Index (https://www.index-space.org/) is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.

We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.

garden3d TK (https://feed.garden3d.net/) — Media

At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone (https://www.thelightphone.com/)
Mill (https://www.mill.com/)
IngredientAI (https://ingredient-ai.com/)

⛰️ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates

️ Systems that hold up

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

Special Projects

In addition to day to day responsibilities, here’s an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years →

• Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts

• Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from

• Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do

• Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio

• Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products

• Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed

Qualifications

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:

Must have:

• 12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company

• Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products

• A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native

• A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure

• All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase

• Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it

• Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients

• A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them

• Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)

Nice-to-have:

• A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products

• Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)

• Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role

• Open source projects they've started or maintained

• Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams

• Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company

• A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring

• Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality

Who you are

The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart” by carefully managing their workflow and team.

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

Compensation

This is a permanent leadership role. If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.

We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $110 - $175 p/hr pending seniority & experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval.

At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators.

‍ How we work:

We believe that there’s a better balance between the poles of freelancing & full time, and for that reason we work differently to most shops:

• Transparency & Ownership (https://sanctucompu.substack.com/p/our-open-source-2020-profit-and-loss): We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. We’re proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.

• 150% Carbon Negative (https://negative.sanctuary.computer/): Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same. We have been certified climate neutral since 2021 (https://twitter.com/sanctucompu/status/1385282161197060100).

• Strong Morals (https://sanctucompu.substack.com/p/our-moral-compass): Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative).

• Async & Decentralized: We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.

• Remote Friendly: Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process.

• Ideas & Products: In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?

→ Read more on our Substack, over here (https://sanctucompu.substack.com/).

How to apply

We’re excited to hear from you! ❤

Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process.

Our team carefully reviews every complete submission, and we truly appreciate the time and effort you put into applying! :)

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/sanctuary-computer-head-of-technology

title: Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA (IA conversationnelle)
description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote)

Upgrade aide ses clients à avancer dans la bonne direction grâce à des produits financiers abordables et responsables. Depuis 2017, nous avons aidé plus de 7,5 millions de clients à accéder à plus de 42 milliards de dollars en crédit à la consommation. En nous concentrant sans relâche sur l'amélioration du bien-être financier de nos clients, nous développons des produits qui leur permettent de faire des économies et qui les soutiennent pour un meilleur avenir financier. Nous sommes soutenus par certains des meilleurs investisseurs dans le domaine de la technologie et avons été récemment valorisés à 7,3 milliards de dollars.

Nous sommes constamment reconnus pour notre culture de collaboration et d'inclusion. Plus récemment, nous avons été classés parmi les Premières entreprises fintech au monde par CNBC, Meilleurs lieux de travail par Built In, et par le San Francisco Business Times, Meilleurs lieux de travail d'Amérique par Newsweek, Meilleur employeur ''Startup'' par Forbes, et Employeurs les plus sains par Phoenix Business Journal.

Nous recherchons de nouveaux membres d'équipe qui sont enthousiastes à l'idée de concevoir et de proposer des produits nouveaux et meilleurs. Rejoignez-nous et aidez à bâtir un meilleur avenir financier pour des millions de personnes.

À propos du rôle

Un(e) Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA est responsable du cycle de vie complet des parcours que nos clients vivent avec l'agent IA d'Upgrade par clavardage, par téléphone et par courriel : création, optimisation, gestion des cas particuliers et augmentation du taux de résolution autonome. Cette personne conçoit des parcours dans les outils sans code de Sierra, collabore avec les groupes produits d'Upgrade pour intégrer leurs processus de service à l'agent, et répond de la capacité de l'agent à résoudre le problème du client de façon sécuritaire, exacte et sans intervention humaine.

Nous recherchons un(e) Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA pour prendre en charge l'agent IA d'Upgrade destiné à la clientèle. Vous ferez le lien entre les équipes de développement, de produit et des opérations clientèle. Vous transformerez des processus de service, comme effectuer un paiement, consulter les détails d'un prêt, mettre à jour une adresse ou activer les paiements préautorisés, en parcours de production, et vous continuerez à les améliorer après leur lancement.

Vous concevrez et gérerez les parcours de A à Z, de la première ébauche jusqu'à leur pleine maturité. Le travail est à la fois celui d'un bâtisseur et d'un analyste : concevoir le parcours, gérer les cas particuliers, lire les transcriptions et augmenter continuellement le taux de résolution autonome. Le taux de résolution autonome, la satisfaction client (CSAT), la qualité des transferts et le taux d'hallucination sont vos indicateurs clés. Au cours de votre première année, vous serez responsable d'un portefeuille de parcours couvrant l'ensemble de nos produits (prêts personnels, carte, paiement différé (BNPL), marge de crédit hypothécaire (HELOC), dépôts) et contribuerez à établir les normes selon lesquelles Upgrade conçoit, teste et déploie ses expériences IA.

Nos technologies principales

Sierra Agent Studio (parcours sans code), simulations et analyse des conversations Sierra, API GraphQL et REST (comme outils de parcours), Genesys (transfert vers le centre de contact), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, Claude et autres outils de LLM.

Ce que vous ferez

• Création de parcours : Concevoir et développer des parcours Sierra dans Agent Studio pour le clavardage, la voix et le courriel, de la phase de découverte avec les opérations jusqu'au déploiement en production

• Optimisation : Analyser chaque semaine les transcriptions, les enregistrements et les données analytiques, repérer où les conversations échouent ou sont transférées, et déployer des correctifs à la logique des parcours, aux instructions et à la base de connaissances

• Gestion des cas particuliers : Cartographier les scénarios problématiques (paiements refusés, identité non concordante, comptes en souffrance, demandes non prises en charge) et s'assurer que chacun se conclut par une réponse exacte ou un transfert fluide

• Résolution autonome : Assumer la responsabilité des cibles de résolution autonome et de CSAT pour chaque parcours, mener des déploiements progressifs (1 % → 100 %) et prioriser les travaux ayant le plus d'impact sur ces indicateurs

• Partenariat produit : Collaborer avec les groupes produits (prêts personnels, carte, BNPL, dépôts) pour définir la portée de nouveaux parcours, maintenir les parcours à jour au fil de l'évolution des produits et définir les API dont l'agent a besoin

• Sécurité et conformité : Appliquer l'authentification à plusieurs niveaux et la vérification renforcée, le libellé de conformité exact ainsi que des garde-fous contre les hallucinations et les réponses non conformes aux politiques

• Transferts : Concevoir les transferts vers des agents humains dans Genesys avec des résumés exacts et le contexte d'authentification

• Tests : Créer des suites de simulation et de tests de régression afin que chaque modification de parcours soit déployée avec la preuve qu'elle n'altère pas le comportement existant

• Surveillance : Suivre la latence, les erreurs et les abandons dans SumoLogic et Grafana, et être responsable des alertes

• Optimisation vocale : Latence, phrases de transition, interruptions, personnalité et ton

• Relation avec Sierra : Agir à titre de responsable technique de notre côté, faire remonter les problèmes liés à la plateforme et orienter les demandes relatives à la feuille de route

Ce que nous recherchons

• De 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en développement logiciel, ou une expérience équivalente dans des rôles en solutions techniques, en IA conversationnelle ou en gestion de produits techniques

• Connaissance pratique du comportement des agents LLM : instructions, appels d'outils, récupération de connaissances, et les points de défaillance de chacun

• Expérience dans la conception d'évaluations pour des systèmes non déterministes : jeux de tests, simulations, LLM évaluateur (LLM-as-judge), seuils de régression

• Une maîtrise technique suffisante pour lire des spécifications d'API, collaborer avec des développeurs backend sur des intégrations REST et GraphQL, et raisonner sur les autorisations et les portées de permissions

• Un esprit axé sur le produit et le client : vous comprenez les procédures opérationnelles, lisez les transcriptions, accordez de l'importance au ton et mesurez votre réussite selon la résolution du problème du client

• Sens des responsabilités en production : déploiements, surveillance, analyse de journaux et réponse aux incidents

• Rédaction claire et capacité à travailler avec des interlocuteurs non techniques des équipes des opérations, de la conformité et des affaires juridiques

Atouts supplémentaires

• Expérience pratique de Sierra Agent Studio ou d'une plateforme d'agents sans code comparable (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect)

• Expérience en IA vocale : reconnaissance vocale (speech-to-text), synthèse vocale (text-to-speech), optimisation de la latence, gestion des interruptions (barge-in)

• Connaissance des systèmes de centre de contact tels que Genesys et de la conception de transferts vers des agents

• Expérience en fintech ou dans un autre secteur réglementé (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2)

• Expérience en conception conversationnelle ou en rédaction UX

Ce que nous vous offrons

• Salaire compétitif ($140K-$180K) et plan d'options d'achat d'actions

• Assurances médicales, dentaires et de la vue payées par l'entreprise

• Congés payés flexibles

• Possibilités de croissance et de développement professionnel

• Congé parental payé

• Initiatives de santé et de bien-être

Exigence linguistique

English language is required for this position, as it involves interacting with staff at Upgrade's offices worldwide.

L'anglais est requis pour ce poste, puisqu'il comporte des interactions avec le personnel des bureaux d'Upgrade à l'échelle internationale.

Conditions environnementales et de travail

Le travail s'effectue à l'intérieur dans un environnement au rythme soutenu qui exige la capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités et de respecter les processus de travail, les horaires et les attentes en matière de service établi.

Les employés saisissent, extraient et échangent régulièrement des informations avec précision à l'aide de systèmes et d'applications numériques afin d'appuyer les objectifs opérationnels et de service à la clientèle.

Le poste exige la capacité de recevoir et d'échanger des informations avec les clients, les collègues, les superviseurs et les partenaires interfonctionnels par le biais des moyens de communication disponibles, qui peuvent inclure des réunions, des courriels, des appels téléphoniques et des outils de collaboration numériques, et peut impliquer des échanges en temps réel, verbaux ou en personne selon les besoins de l'entreprise.

Les fonctions peuvent inclure la gestion d'un volume élevé d'interactions entrantes et/ou sortantes avec la clientèle ainsi que d'activités de travail à l'aide de systèmes de télécommunication et informatiques. Le poste exige la capacité de lire, d'analyser et d'interpréter les informations affichées à l'écran d'ordinateur et de maintenir une posture de travail pendant de longues périodes, conformément aux exigences du poste.

Le travail peut s'effectuer dans un centre de contact, un bureau ou en télétravail, selon les besoins de l'entreprise et la nature du poste. Les environnements de travail sur place peuvent inclure des espaces de travail partagés, un éclairage de bureau standard et un bruit de fond modéré typique des environnements de service à la clientèle ou opérationnels.

Les employés en télétravail sont responsables de maintenir un espace de travail sécurisé et productif avec une connexion Internet fiable qui prend en charge les systèmes de l'entreprise et protège la confidentialité des informations de l'entreprise et des clients.

Des mesures d'adaptation raisonnables peuvent être mises en place pour permettre aux personnes qualifiées vivant avec un handicap d'exercer les fonctions essentielles du poste, conformément à l'Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) et aux lois étatiques et locales applicables.

Nous sommes un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances et nous valorisons la diversité au sein de notre entreprise. Nous ne faisons pas de discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion, la couleur, l'origine nationale, le sexe, l'orientation sexuelle, l'âge, l'état civil, le statut d'ancien combattant ou le statut de handicap.

Upgrade n'accepte pas les candidatures spontanées soumises par des agences de recrutement, des cabinets de recherche de personnel ou toute autre tierce partie. Tout CV soumis à un employé d'Upgrade sans accord écrit préalable en vigueur sera considéré comme la propriété d'Upgrade, et Upgrade ne sera pas tenue de payer des bonus de recommandation ou de placement. Les agences doivent obtenir une approbation écrite au préalable du service d'acquisition de talents d'Upgrade pour soumettre des candidatures, et ce, seulement si une entente valide et dûment signée est en vigueur.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/upgrade-developpeur-euse-experience-ia-ia-conversationnelle
