Nous recherchons un(e) Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA pour prendre en charge l'agent IA d'Upgrade destiné à la clientèle. Vous ferez le lien entre les équipes de développement, de produit et des opérations clientèle. Vous transformerez des processus de service, comme effectuer un paiement, consulter les détails d'un prêt, mettre à jour une adresse ou activer les paiements préautorisés, en parcours de production, et vous continuerez à les améliorer après leur lancement.

Vous concevrez et gérerez les parcours de A à Z, de la première ébauche jusqu'à leur pleine maturité. Le travail est à la fois celui d'un bâtisseur et d'un analyste : concevoir le parcours, gérer les cas particuliers, lire les transcriptions et augmenter continuellement le taux de résolution autonome. Le taux de résolution autonome, la satisfaction client (CSAT), la qualité des transferts et le taux d'hallucination sont vos indicateurs clés. Au cours de votre première année, vous serez responsable d'un portefeuille de parcours couvrant l'ensemble de nos produits (prêts personnels, carte, paiement différé (BNPL), marge de crédit hypothécaire (HELOC), dépôts) et contribuerez à établir les normes selon lesquelles Upgrade conçoit, teste et déploie ses expériences IA.

Nos technologies principales

Sierra Agent Studio (parcours sans code), simulations et analyse des conversations Sierra, API GraphQL et REST (comme outils de parcours), Genesys (transfert vers le centre de contact), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, Claude et autres outils de LLM.

Ce que vous ferez

• Création de parcours : Concevoir et développer des parcours Sierra dans Agent Studio pour le clavardage, la voix et le courriel, de la phase de découverte avec les opérations jusqu'au déploiement en production

• Optimisation : Analyser chaque semaine les transcriptions, les enregistrements et les données analytiques, repérer où les conversations échouent ou sont transférées, et déployer des correctifs à la logique des parcours, aux instructions et à la base de connaissances

• Gestion des cas particuliers : Cartographier les scénarios problématiques (paiements refusés, identité non concordante, comptes en souffrance, demandes non prises en charge) et s'assurer que chacun se conclut par une réponse exacte ou un transfert fluide

• Résolution autonome : Assumer la responsabilité des cibles de résolution autonome et de CSAT pour chaque parcours, mener des déploiements progressifs (1 % → 100 %) et prioriser les travaux ayant le plus d'impact sur ces indicateurs

• Partenariat produit : Collaborer avec les groupes produits (prêts personnels, carte, BNPL, dépôts) pour définir la portée de nouveaux parcours, maintenir les parcours à jour au fil de l'évolution des produits et définir les API dont l'agent a besoin

• Sécurité et conformité : Appliquer l'authentification à plusieurs niveaux et la vérification renforcée, le libellé de conformité exact ainsi que des garde-fous contre les hallucinations et les réponses non conformes aux politiques

• Transferts : Concevoir les transferts vers des agents humains dans Genesys avec des résumés exacts et le contexte d'authentification

• Tests : Créer des suites de simulation et de tests de régression afin que chaque modification de parcours soit déployée avec la preuve qu'elle n'altère pas le comportement existant

• Surveillance : Suivre la latence, les erreurs et les abandons dans SumoLogic et Grafana, et être responsable des alertes

• Optimisation vocale : Latence, phrases de transition, interruptions, personnalité et ton

• Relation avec Sierra : Agir à titre de responsable technique de notre côté, faire remonter les problèmes liés à la plateforme et orienter les demandes relatives à la feuille de route

Ce que nous recherchons

• De 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en développement logiciel, ou une expérience équivalente dans des rôles en solutions techniques, en IA conversationnelle ou en gestion de produits techniques

• Connaissance pratique du comportement des agents LLM : instructions, appels d'outils, récupération de connaissances, et les points de défaillance de chacun

• Expérience dans la conception d'évaluations pour des systèmes non déterministes : jeux de tests, simulations, LLM évaluateur (LLM-as-judge), seuils de régression

• Une maîtrise technique suffisante pour lire des spécifications d'API, collaborer avec des développeurs backend sur des intégrations REST et GraphQL, et raisonner sur les autorisations et les portées de permissions

• Un esprit axé sur le produit et le client : vous comprenez les procédures opérationnelles, lisez les transcriptions, accordez de l'importance au ton et mesurez votre réussite selon la résolution du problème du client

• Sens des responsabilités en production : déploiements, surveillance, analyse de journaux et réponse aux incidents

• Rédaction claire et capacité à travailler avec des interlocuteurs non techniques des équipes des opérations, de la conformité et des affaires juridiques

Atouts supplémentaires

• Expérience pratique de Sierra Agent Studio ou d'une plateforme d'agents sans code comparable (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect)

• Expérience en IA vocale : reconnaissance vocale (speech-to-text), synthèse vocale (text-to-speech), optimisation de la latence, gestion des interruptions (barge-in)

• Connaissance des systèmes de centre de contact tels que Genesys et de la conception de transferts vers des agents

• Expérience en fintech ou dans un autre secteur réglementé (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2)

• Expérience en conception conversationnelle ou en rédaction UX

Ce que nous vous offrons

• Salaire compétitif ($140K-$180K) et plan d'options d'achat d'actions

• Assurances médicales, dentaires et de la vue payées par l'entreprise

• Congés payés flexibles

• Possibilités de croissance et de développement professionnel

• Congé parental payé

• Initiatives de santé et de bien-être

Exigence linguistique

English language is required for this position, as it involves interacting with staff at Upgrade's offices worldwide.

L'anglais est requis pour ce poste, puisqu'il comporte des interactions avec le personnel des bureaux d'Upgrade à l'échelle internationale.

Conditions environnementales et de travail

Le travail s'effectue à l'intérieur dans un environnement au rythme soutenu qui exige la capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités et de respecter les processus de travail, les horaires et les attentes en matière de service établi.

Les employés saisissent, extraient et échangent régulièrement des informations avec précision à l'aide de systèmes et d'applications numériques afin d'appuyer les objectifs opérationnels et de service à la clientèle.

Le poste exige la capacité de recevoir et d'échanger des informations avec les clients, les collègues, les superviseurs et les partenaires interfonctionnels par le biais des moyens de communication disponibles, qui peuvent inclure des réunions, des courriels, des appels téléphoniques et des outils de collaboration numériques, et peut impliquer des échanges en temps réel, verbaux ou en personne selon les besoins de l'entreprise.

Les fonctions peuvent inclure la gestion d'un volume élevé d'interactions entrantes et/ou sortantes avec la clientèle ainsi que d'activités de travail à l'aide de systèmes de télécommunication et informatiques. Le poste exige la capacité de lire, d'analyser et d'interpréter les informations affichées à l'écran d'ordinateur et de maintenir une posture de travail pendant de longues périodes, conformément aux exigences du poste.

Le travail peut s'effectuer dans un centre de contact, un bureau ou en télétravail, selon les besoins de l'entreprise et la nature du poste. Les environnements de travail sur place peuvent inclure des espaces de travail partagés, un éclairage de bureau standard et un bruit de fond modéré typique des environnements de service à la clientèle ou opérationnels.

Les employés en télétravail sont responsables de maintenir un espace de travail sécurisé et productif avec une connexion Internet fiable qui prend en charge les systèmes de l'entreprise et protège la confidentialité des informations de l'entreprise et des clients.

Des mesures d'adaptation raisonnables peuvent être mises en place pour permettre aux personnes qualifiées vivant avec un handicap d'exercer les fonctions essentielles du poste, conformément à l'Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) et aux lois étatiques et locales applicables.

Nous sommes un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances et nous valorisons la diversité au sein de notre entreprise. Nous ne faisons pas de discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion, la couleur, l'origine nationale, le sexe, l'orientation sexuelle, l'âge, l'état civil, le statut d'ancien combattant ou le statut de handicap.

Upgrade n'accepte pas les candidatures spontanées soumises par des agences de recrutement, des cabinets de recherche de personnel ou toute autre tierce partie. Tout CV soumis à un employé d'Upgrade sans accord écrit préalable en vigueur sera considéré comme la propriété d'Upgrade, et Upgrade ne sera pas tenue de payer des bonus de recommandation ou de placement. Les agences doivent obtenir une approbation écrite au préalable du service d'acquisition de talents d'Upgrade pour soumettre des candidatures, et ce, seulement si une entente valide et dûment signée est en vigueur.

title: Engineering Manager
description:
Headquarters: London

URL: http://www.medify.co.uk

Remote | Full-Time | UK

About Us

At Medify, we’re on a mission to widen access to medicine and healthcare careers through world-class digital learning experiences. Since 2009, we’ve helped thousands of students prepare for high-stakes admissions tests, and we’re continuing to invest in our technology to build innovative, scalable products that support learners around the world.

As we continue to grow, we’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead, mentor and develop our engineering team while remaining hands-on in building the platform that powers Medify.

The Role

As an Engineering Manager, you’ll play a pivotal role in shaping both our engineering culture and technical direction. Working closely with the CTO, Product and Design teams, you’ll lead a team of talented full-stack engineers, helping them grow while ensuring we continue to deliver high-quality software that delights our users.

This is a hands-on leadership role, with at least 50% of your time dedicated to engineering. You’ll contribute across the full software development lifecycle - from architecture and design through to development, testing and deployment - while driving engineering excellence and fostering a collaborative, high-performing team.

Our current technology stack includes Ruby on Rails, React, PostgreSQL, with infrastructure transitioning from Heroku to AWS.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead, mentor and support a team of full-stack engineers through coaching, regular 1:1s and performance reviews.

• Foster a culture of continuous learning, collaboration and technical excellence.

• Support career development, engagement and long-term capability building across the engineering team.

• Contribute to hiring by supporting interviews and recruitment of exceptional engineering talent.

• Design, develop and maintain scalable, high-quality software solutions.

• Collaborate closely with Product and Design teams to translate requirements into technical solutions.

• Participate in architectural decisions and help shape the future of the Medify platform.

• Conduct thoughtful code reviews and promote engineering best practices.

• Troubleshoot and resolve software issues while maintaining high standards of reliability and performance.

• Develop automated tests and contribute to a robust testing culture.

• Participate in agile planning, backlog refinement and sprint delivery.

• Stay up to date with emerging technologies and identify opportunities to improve our engineering practices.

About You

You’ll be a technically strong engineering leader who enjoys developing people just as much as building great software. You’re comfortable balancing strategic leadership with hands-on development and thrive in a fast-moving, collaborative environment.

You’ll ideally have:

• 2+ years’ experience leading or managing software engineering teams.

• 5+ years’ experience in software development.

• Strong experience with modern software engineering practices and frameworks.

• Experience with Ruby on Rails and React (highly desirable).

• A proven track record of building scalable, maintainable software.

• Experience working in Agile development environments.

• Experience collaborating with cross-functional Product and Design teams.

• Experience recruiting, mentoring and developing engineers.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• Excellent problem-solving ability with a focus on quality and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

• Degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline is desirable, but not essential.

Technical Skills

• Strong knowledge of modern programming languages and software frameworks.

• Excellent understanding of software architecture, design principles, data structures and algorithms.

• Experience working with relational databases, APIs and networking.

• Knowledge of automated testing frameworks and software quality practices.

• Familiarity with DevOps tools and deployment pipelines.

• Ability to quickly learn and adopt new technologies.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills.

✅ What We Offer

• Fully remote working with flexibility and autonomy.

• The opportunity to shape the future of Medify’s technology platform.

• A supportive, collaborative engineering culture that values continuous learning.

• A hands-on leadership role with real technical influence.

• The opportunity to work on products that positively impact thousands of aspiring healthcare professionals every year.

• Competitive salary and benefits package.

title: IT Support Specialist
description:
Headquarters: United States, Remote

Our Mission:

6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency.  We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

Our People:

People are the heart and soul of 6sense. We serve with passion and purpose. We live by our Being 6sense values of Win as One Team, Stay Curious, Do The Right Thing, Own the Outcome, and Create Belonging.  Every 6sensor plays a part in deﬁning the future of our industry-leading technology.  6sense is a place where difference-makers roll up their sleeves, take risks, act with integrity, and measure success by the value we create for our customers.  We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career.

IT Support Specialist

About the Role

6sense is looking for an IT Support Specialist who is passionate about delivering exceptional employee experiences through world-class IT support. This role combines hands-on end user support with administration of modern workplace technologies, identity systems, SaaS applications, endpoint management, and AI platforms.

You'll support a global workforce while helping improve IT operations through automation, documentation, and process improvement. We're looking for someone who enjoys solving problems, learning new technologies, and creating scalable solutions that make employees more productive.

What You'll Do

• Provide Tier 1 and Tier 2 support through tickets, chat, email, and remote support sessions.

• Support macOS, Windows 11, Microsoft 365, Teams, Slack, and Zoom environments.

• Manage user lifecycle processes including onboarding, offboarding, access requests, and role changes.

• Administer and troubleshoot Okta, Entra ID, SSO, MFA, and identity-related services.

• Support and manage SaaS platforms including Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom, 1Password, GitHub, Claude Enterprise, and Workato.

• Deploy, configure, and maintain endpoints using Intune, Iru, and CrowdStrike.

• Maintain accurate asset inventory and device lifecycle management.

• Support Microsoft Copilot, Claude, and other AI technologies while promoting responsible AI practices.

• Develop scripts, automations, and workflow improvements that reduce manual effort and improve efficiency.

• Create and maintain documentation, knowledge articles, and standard operating procedures.

• Provide occasional support for Zoom Rooms, Teams meetings, executive users, and company events.

What We're Looking For

• 3+ years of experience in IT Support, Help Desk, Service Desk, or End User Computing.

• Experience supporting macOS and Windows environments.

• Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Teams, Slack, and Zoom.

• Familiarity with identity and access management concepts including Okta, Entra ID, SSO, and MFA.

• Experience with endpoint management tools such as Intune, Iru, or similar MDM platforms.

• Strong troubleshooting, communication, and customer service skills.

• Experience working in a fast-paced, remote-first environment.

• Basic scripting or automation experience using PowerShell, Bash, Python, Workato, or similar tools.

• Interest in AI technologies such as Microsoft Copilot and Claude.

• Strong attention to detail, ownership, and a continuous improvement mindset.

Bonus Points

• Experience administering Okta, Entra ID, Intune, or Iru.

• Experience with Workato or workflow automation platforms.

• Experience supporting AI platforms and governance practices.

• ITIL, Okta, Microsoft, Apple, or security-related certifications.

• Experience supporting executive stakeholders and globally distributed teams.

Success in This Role

You'll thrive in this role if you're customer-obsessed, highly organized, technically curious, and motivated to improve how IT services are delivered. Success will be measured through service quality, SLA performance, knowledge sharing, asset management accuracy, and contributions to automation and process improvement.

Base Salary Range: $73,577.25 - $103,913.30. The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high end of the base salary range for this position. Actual salaries may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors, including but not limited to work location and experience. The base salary is one component of 6sense’s total compensation package for this position. Other compensation may include a bonus program or commission plan, and stock options if approved by 6sense’s board. In addition, 6sense provides a variety of benefits, including generous health insurance coverage, life, and disability insurance, a 401K employer matching program, paid holidays, self-care days, and paid time off (PTO). #Li-remote

Notice of Collection and Use of Personal Information for California Residents: California Recruitment Privacy Notice and Policy (https://6sense.com/california-recruitment-privacy-notice/)

Our Benefits:

Full-time employees can take advantage of health coverage, paid parental leave, generous paid time-off and holidays, quarterly self-care days off, and stock options. We’ll make sure you have the equipment and support you need to work and connect with your teams, at home or in one of our oﬃces.

We have a growth mindset culture that is represented in all that we do, from onboarding through to numerous learning and development initiatives including access to our LinkedIn Learning platform. Employee well-being is also top of mind for us. We host quarterly wellness education sessions to encourage self care and personal growth. From wellness days to ERG-hosted events, we celebrate and energize all 6sense employees and their backgrounds.

Equal Opportunity Employer:

6sense is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employers. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to jobs@6sense.com.

We are aware of recruiting impersonation attempts that are not affiliated with 6sense in any way. All email communications from 6sense will originate from the @6sense.com domain. We will not initially contact you via text message and will never request payments. If you are uncertain whether you have been contacted by an official 6sense employee, reach out to jobs@6sense.com

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/6sense-it-support-specialist

title: Enterprise Sales Director
description:
Headquarters: Remote, Massachusetts, United States, AMER

From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us
Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role
We’re looking to hire a Sales Director to join the Revenue Team in Boston, MA. This person will be responsible for building out our enterprise customer base. The ideal person will be a proactive and curious member of our growing Sales team, identifying new business with prospects and growth opportunities for clients. A certain level of foresight and knowledge working with intrinsic sales cycles will take this individual confidently into the future of dbt Labs.

What You'll Do

• Own the full sales cycle from lead to ongoing utilization for enterprise prospects

• Organize POC implementations of dbt Cloud Enterprise

• Win 20 new dbt Cloud Enterprise customers per year (after ramp)

• Lead and contribute to team projects that develop our sales process

• Work with product to build and maintain the dbt Cloud enterprise roadmap

• Become an expert in SQL, dbt, and enterprise data operations

• Be an active member of the dbt open source community

Skills We’re Looking For

• 6+ years closing experience in technology sales, with 2+ years of experience in enterprise sales.

• Ability to understand complex technical concepts and develop them into a consultative sale

• Excellent verbal, written, and in-person communication skills to engage stakeholders at all levels of an analytics organization (individual developer up to CTO)

• The diligence and organizational skills to work long, intricate sales cycles involving multiple client teams

• Ability to operate in an ambiguous and fast-paced work environment

• A passion for being an inclusive teammate and involved member of the community

• Experience with SQL or willingness to learn

Bonus Skills​

• Prior experience in analytics, ETL, BI, and/or open-sourced software

• Knowledge of or prior experience with dbt

The compensation range displayed on this job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire compensation for the target position and level, and may include sales incentives or target bonuses depending on the role.  Our compensation ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Our job titles may span more than one career level. Within the range, individual compensation is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, relevant education or training, business need, market demands. The compensation range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. Your recruiter can share more about the specific compensation range for your location during the hiring process.

Pay Range

$142,486—$178,107.75 USD

OTE (On Target Earning)

$284,972—$356,215.50 USD

Perks and Benefits

• 100% employer-paid medical insurance*

• Generous paid time away from work, including paid vacation or flexible/unlimited vacation depending on role and country, plus paid sick time, inclusive parental leave, paid holidays, including a year-end Global Week of Rest, and volunteer days off.

• RSU stock grants*

• Professional development and training opportunities

• Company virtual happy hours, free food, and fun team-building activities

• Monthly cell phone stipend

• Access to an innovative mental health support platform that offers personalized care and resources in areas such as: therapy, coaching, and self-guided mindfulness exercises for all covered employees and their covered dependents.

*May vary by country and worker type - please reach out to your recruiter for more information

Click here (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CdawUwjo1Q1B7ghZJ_owdmmHB8VtqhBu?usp=sharing) to learn more about Fivetran's Benefits by Region.

We’re honored to be valued at over $5.6 billion (https://fivetran.com/blog/hvr-acquisition-series-d), but more importantly, we’re proud of our core values of Get Stuck In, Do the Right Thing, and One Team, One Dream (https://fivetran.com/culture). Read about us in Forbes (https://fivetran-com.s3.amazonaws.com/news/forbes-aug-sept-2022-digital-reprint-10-21-22.pdf).

Fivetran brings together high-quality talent across the globe to make data access as easy and reliable as electricity for our customers. We value and recognize that our customers benefit from having innovative teams made of people from many backgrounds, experiences, and identities. Fivetran promotes diversity, equity, inclusion & belonging through attracting, recruiting, developing, and retaining a diverse workforce, not only because it is the right thing to do, but because it helps us build a world-class company to better serve our customers, our people and our communities.

title: CRM/ CVM / Lifecycle/Retention Marketing Lead (US b2c subscription only)
description:
Headquarters: Bulgaria

URL: http://jobhire.ai

Description
CVM Lead (US Market)

Location: Remote

Job Type: Full-time

About JobHire.AI (http://JobHire.AI)

JobHire.AI (http://JobHire.AI) is a vertical AI agent that automates job search for professionals in the US market. We find, tailor, and apply to jobs on behalf of thousands of paying subscribers — at scale and with precision. We operate a subscription model with monthly and longer-term tiers, plus paid add-ons. We're entering a phase where deeper customer value management — not just acquisition — is the single biggest unlock for profitable growth.

Why This Role Now

We are spending efficiently to acquire users — but a substantial portion of revenue is left on the table after the first purchase. Reg→Purchase conversion is below where it should be. Rebill rates erode quickly past month one. Add-on attach is minimal. Our reactivation engine is currently offline. We've been operating an email-only CRM on a platform that doesn't return analytics through its API.

That ends with this hire. This is a role for someone who has already done the transformation we need: turning a basic broadcast CRM into a measurable CVM function that drives incremental revenue across email, SMS, and web push — on the US market specifically.

What You'll Own

Funnel Conversion

• Drive Reg→Purchase conversion through triggered post-quiz, paywall-abandonment, and onboarding sequences across email, SMS, and web push.

• Own first-purchase activation across the first 7 days.

Retention & Rebill

• Differentiate renewal sequences by plan tier (1 / 3 / 6 month).

• Build pre-cancel intervention flows — pause offer, plan-switch, value reminder — using captured cancel reason.

• Move the dial on month-1 rebill rate, the single most leveraged metric in our subscription economics.

Reactivation

• Build the reactivation engine for the cancelled cohort — across email and SMS, personalized by cancel reason and tenure.

• Recover revenue from a base that is currently dormant due to deliverability issues.

Add-on Monetization

• Own the CRM-driven path to add-on products (Resume Review, Resume Builder): timing, segmentation, copy, channel.

Channel & Tooling

• Lead the migration off our current ESP onto our chosen omnichannel platform (Maestra is the current candidate; Customer.io (http://Customer.io) is the alternative).

• Recover and maintain email domain reputation.

• Stand up SMS as a first-class channel — including US compliance (TCPA, A2P 10DLC).

• Stand up web push and orchestrate cross-channel flows (email → SMS → push cascades).

Measurement

• Implement incremental measurement with holdouts on every flow. We don't want activity reports — we want incremental revenue, attributable and defensible.

Expected Outcomes

First 3 Months

• Email deliverability restored to historical baseline.

• Reactivation campaign launched with measurable incremental conversion against a holdout.

• Differentiated renewal flows live for 1 / 3 / 6 month plans.

• Decision (signed off with engineering) on omnichannel platform: migrate to Maestra or alternative.

First 6 Months

• SMS and web push live as ongoing production channels in lifecycle flows.

• Measurable lift in Reg→Purchase conversion via paywall-abandonment and post-registration triggered sequences.

• Measurable lift in month-1 rebill rate via differentiated and intervention flows.

• Add-on attach rate (Resume Review, Resume Builder) materially up via CRM-driven sales sequences.

• Per-flow incremental revenue reported weekly via proper holdout methodology.

12 Months

• CVM channel contributing as a top-3 incremental revenue source for the company.

• Cross-channel lifecycle strategy (email + SMS + web push + iMessage/RCS as those channels mature in the US) live and documented.

• Process documentation and tooling stable enough to remove key-person risk.

We keep our hiring process quick and simple:

• HR Introduction Call

• Team Interviews

• Challenge

• Reference Check (with three prior managers)

Requirements
You're a Fit If You Have

• 3+ years operating CVM/lifecycle programs on the US market specifically. US b2c subscription. This is non-negotiable — US deliverability, US carriers, US consumer behavior, US compliance.

• 5+ years total in CRM / lifecycle / CVM, with at least one stint owning the function end-to-end (not just executing).

• Hands-on operating experience with an enterprise omnichannel platform — Maestra strongly preferred; Braze, Iterable, Customer.io (http://Customer.io), or Klaviyo also relevant.

• Real, hands-on experience launching SMS as a marketing channel in the US (TCPA, A2P 10DLC, carrier compliance — not "I worked with a vendor who handled it").

• Real, hands-on experience launching web push and measuring its lift.

• SQL good enough to pull your own segments and validate your own data.

• A subscription-business orientation: you think in LTV/payer, payback period, retention curves, and cohorts — not in opens and clicks.

• A track record of measurable incremental revenue from CRM, ideally validated through holdout.

• Bias toward action. We operate as a tiny team; you'll need to ship faster than you plan.

Nice to Have

• Experience migrating off a damaged email domain.

• Experience in job search, career, HR-tech, or adjacent consumer subscription verticals (EdTech, FinTech, dating, streaming).

• iMessage Business / RCS experience.

• Communication (speak English and Russian).

Benefits

• Clear mandate and ownership from day one. You're the function, not a contributor to it.

• The economics are highly leveraged — even a 5-percentage-point lift on month-1 rebill is meaningful to the bottom line of the company.

• Direct work with the CMO, CEO, and Growth PM. No layers, no politics.

• A market where your work is directly visible to users searching for their next job — outcomes you can feel.

• $4000-7000/month + 38DaysOff.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/jobhire-crm-cvm-lifecycle-retention-marketing-lead-us-b2c-subscription-only

title: Software Engineer AI Coding Tasks
description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works

• Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.

• Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.

• Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.

• Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.

• Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.

• Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.

• Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

Requirements

• 2+ years of professional software engineering

• Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)

• Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++

• Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing

• Regular use of an AI coding tool

• Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models

• You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words

• At least 10 hours a week, starting now

• A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

Nice to have

• Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure

• Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

Terms

• US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you

• Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms

• The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

• Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

title: Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI
description:
Headquarters: Remote, United States

Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI

REMOTE, United States

JOB OVERVIEW

Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it.

Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. The more substantial problem — software that reasons over demand, labor regulation, and employee preferences, then acts, with a person in the loop wherever the stakes require one — remains unsolved across the category. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there.

You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion's AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it.

Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not.

The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem.

Build quality. You are accountable for what ships, not for what was specified. That means staying engaged through implementation: reviewing the build against the specification as it comes together, using the product yourself before anyone else is asked to, joining bug triage and design review, catching drift from intent while it is still cheap to correct, and holding a release when the quality is not there. Our customers experience the build, not the document. A well-written specification that produced a product managers do not trust is failed product work, and we assess it that way.

Evaluation. Build and maintain the evaluation sets that determine whether an agent is ready to ship and whether it is degrading in production — writing the cases, reviewing failure traces, setting the pass criteria. You will be the person who holds a release when the demonstration is persuasive and the evaluation is not.

Specifications. Legion uses Functional Requirements Documents as its ground-truth specification layer; release notes, enablement material, and sales content are generated from maintained specifications rather than reconstructed from code or institutional memory. Write FRDs that meet that standard and keep them accurate after release. A specification is where the work begins, not where your responsibility ends.

Commercialization. Partner with go-to-market on packaging, metering, pricing inputs, and field readiness. Agentic products raise difficult commercial questions — what unit to meter, what a customer is paying for when software performs work a person previously did — and you will be expected to hold a considered position on them.

Design-partner delivery. Lead agent deployments with large enterprise design partners: scoping the pilot, establishing success criteria before it begins, joining failure reviews, and determining what becomes generally available and what remains bespoke.

TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS

Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves:

• Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior

• Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything

• Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications

• Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation

• Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them

• Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS

• Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone.

• Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters

We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

• 7+ years in product management (Senior) or 10+ years (Principal), including at least 2 years shipping LLM-backed features to external, paying users — not internal tools, proofs of concept, or hackathon projects

• Demonstrated hands-on capability of the kind described above. Expect to show your work.

• Substantial enterprise B2B SaaS experience: multi-tenant architecture, role-based access control, audit trails, single sign-on, data residency, security review, and enterprise procurement. You should be able to anticipate what a customer's security questionnaire will ask about an LLM feature.

• A record of taking an ambiguous, operationally complex domain problem through to a shipped product with demonstrated adoption — not only launch

• Evidence of staying with a product through implementation and owning its quality at release. We will ask about a release you delayed or stopped, what you found, and how you found it.

• The judgment to recognize what current models cannot do reliably, and the willingness to say so when a room expects a different answer

• Comfort working inside a codebase. An engineering background is not required, but you should be able to read the code behind what you are specifying, run it locally, and open a pull request.

• Strong written communication. Legion runs on documents, and candidates are evaluated substantially on how they write.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES

• Direct experience in workforce management, HCM, ERP, supply chain, or another operationally complex enterprise domain with compliance exposure

• Familiarity with labor compliance regimes — predictive scheduling ordinances, meal and rest break rules, union work rules — or demonstrated ability to become fluent in a comparable regulatory domain quickly

• Background in demand forecasting, optimization, or decision systems

• Experience building platform or authoring surfaces that customers configure themselves

• An engineering or technical degree, or prior experience as an engineer or data scientist

• Experience with products sold into frontline-heavy industries: retail, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing

SCOPE OF ROLE, STATED PLAINLY

So that candidates can assess fit early:

• This is an individual contributor role. There is no team to inherit and no management responsibility at present.

• The role is accountable for what ships, not for what is specified. Writing the specification is a portion of the work, not the whole of it.

• This is not an AI strategy or vendor-evaluation role. The work is product definition, prototyping, specification, evaluation, and delivery.

• The role requires forming an independent point of view from operational research. Direction will not be handed down in detail.

• The environment carries genuine ambiguity. The category is being defined as we work in it, and model capabilities shift underneath the roadmap.

SELECTION PROCESS

Our process includes a practical exercise: a sanitized workforce management problem, for which candidates produce an agent design — scope, tools, failure modes, human-in-the-loop contract, and evaluation plan — together with a working prototype they built themselves, using any model provider they prefer. The exercise is then discussed with the people the candidate would work alongside. We weigh it heavily, and we compensate candidates for the time.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Salary Range: $280,000-$300,000 +bonus (tied to business outcomes) +Stock Equity

At Legion, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to all employees. As a fully remote employer, pay for positions is determined using local, national, and industry-specific survey data.

Our posted salary range is done so in good faith based on national data and may be refined for a candidate's region/town/cost of living. We strive to make competitive offers that allow employees room for future growth. Salaries will be based on the applicant’s location, level of experience, education, and specialized knowledge and skills. Additionally, we consider the external market rate, the amount we have budgeted internally, and the internal equity for the same position within the company.

Benefits include, but are not limited to:

• $0 monthly premium and other flexible medical, dental, and vision plans effective on the first day of employment

• 401k plan

• Discretionary Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays

Headquarters: Remote, United States

Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI

REMOTE, United States

JOB OVERVIEW

Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it.

Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. The more substantial problem — software that reasons over demand, labor regulation, and employee preferences, then acts, with a person in the loop wherever the stakes require one — remains unsolved across the category. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there.

You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion's AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it.

Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not.

The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem.

Build quality. You are accountable for what ships, not for what was specified. That means staying engaged through implementation: reviewing the build against the specification as it comes together, using the product yourself before anyone else is asked to, joining bug triage and design review, catching drift from intent while it is still cheap to correct, and holding a release when the quality is not there. Our customers experience the build, not the document. A well-written specification that produced a product managers do not trust is failed product work, and we assess it that way.

Evaluation. Build and maintain the evaluation sets that determine whether an agent is ready to ship and whether it is degrading in production — writing the cases, reviewing failure traces, setting the pass criteria. You will be the person who holds a release when the demonstration is persuasive and the evaluation is not.

Specifications. Legion uses Functional Requirements Documents as its ground-truth specification layer; release notes, enablement material, and sales content are generated from maintained specifications rather than reconstructed from code or institutional memory. Write FRDs that meet that standard and keep them accurate after release. A specification is where the work begins, not where your responsibility ends.

Commercialization. Partner with go-to-market on packaging, metering, pricing inputs, and field readiness. Agentic products raise difficult commercial questions — what unit to meter, what a customer is paying for when software performs work a person previously did — and you will be expected to hold a considered position on them.

Design-partner delivery. Lead agent deployments with large enterprise design partners: scoping the pilot, establishing success criteria before it begins, joining failure reviews, and determining what becomes generally available and what remains bespoke.

TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS

Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves:

• Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior

• Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything

• Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications

• Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation

• Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them

• Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS

• Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone.

• Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters

We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

• 7+ years in product management (Senior) or 10+ years (Principal), including at least 2 years shipping LLM-backed features to external, paying users — not internal tools, proofs of concept, or hackathon projects

• Demonstrated hands-on capability of the kind described above. Expect to show your work.

• Substantial enterprise B2B SaaS experience: multi-tenant architecture, role-based access control, audit trails, single sign-on, data residency, security review, and enterprise procurement. You should be able to anticipate what a customer's security questionnaire will ask about an LLM feature.

• A record of taking an ambiguous, operationally complex domain problem through to a shipped product with demonstrated adoption — not only launch

• Evidence of staying with a product through implementation and owning its quality at release. We will ask about a release you delayed or stopped, what you found, and how you found it.

• The judgment to recognize what current models cannot do reliably, and the willingness to say so when a room expects a different answer

• Comfort working inside a codebase. An engineering background is not required, but you should be able to read the code behind what you are specifying, run it locally, and open a pull request.

• Strong written communication. Legion runs on documents, and candidates are evaluated substantially on how they write.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES

• Direct experience in workforce management, HCM, ERP, supply chain, or another operationally complex enterprise domain with compliance exposure

• Familiarity with labor compliance regimes — predictive scheduling ordinances, meal and rest break rules, union work rules — or demonstrated ability to become fluent in a comparable regulatory domain quickly

• Background in demand forecasting, optimization, or decision systems

• Experience building platform or authoring surfaces that customers configure themselves

• An engineering or technical degree, or prior experience as an engineer or data scientist

• Experience with products sold into frontline-heavy industries: retail, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing

SCOPE OF ROLE, STATED PLAINLY

So that candidates can assess fit early:

• This is an individual contributor role. There is no team to inherit and no management responsibility at present.

• The role is accountable for what ships, not for what is specified. Writing the specification is a portion of the work, not the whole of it.

• This is not an AI strategy or vendor-evaluation role. The work is product definition, prototyping, specification, evaluation, and delivery.

• The role requires forming an independent point of view from operational research. Direction will not be handed down in detail.

• The environment carries genuine ambiguity. The category is being defined as we work in it, and model capabilities shift underneath the roadmap.

SELECTION PROCESS

Our process includes a practical exercise: a sanitized workforce management problem, for which candidates produce an agent design — scope, tools, failure modes, human-in-the-loop contract, and evaluation plan — together with a working prototype they built themselves, using any model provider they prefer. The exercise is then discussed with the people the candidate would work alongside. We weigh it heavily, and we compensate candidates for the time.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES Direct experience in workforce management, HCM, ERP, supply chain, or another operationally complex enterprise domain with compliance exposure Familiarity with labor compliance regimes — predictive scheduling ordinances, meal and rest break rules, union work rules — or demonstrated ability to become fluent in a comparable regulatory domain quickly Background in demand forecasting, optimization, or decision systems Experience building platform or authoring surfaces that customers configure themselves An engineering or technical degree, or prior experience as an engineer or data scientist Experience with products sold into frontline-heavy industries: retail, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing SCOPE OF ROLE, STATED PLAINLY So that candidates can assess fit early: This is an individual contributor role. There is no team to inherit and no management responsibility at present. The role is accountable for what ships, not for what is specified. Writing the specification is a portion of the work, not the whole of it. This is not an AI strategy or vendor-evaluation role. The work is product definition, prototyping, specification, evaluation, and delivery. The role requires forming an independent point of view from operational research. As a fully remote employer, pay for positions is determined using local, national, and industry-specific survey data. Our posted salary range is done so in good faith based on national data and may be refined for a candidate's region/town/cost of living. With us, you'll grow your skills, work closely with experienced executives, and contribute significantly to our mission. Legion Technologies delivers the industry’s most innovative workforce management platform. It enables businesses to maximize labor efficiency and employee engagement simultaneously. The award-winning, AI-driven Legion WFM platform is intelligent, automated, and employee-centric. It’s proven to deliver 13x ROI through schedule optimization, reduced attrition, increased productivity, and increased operational efficiency. title: Customer Value Architect III
description:
Headquarters: Remote, US

About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com (https://mixpanel.com/home/).

About the Team

The Customer Value Architects team sits inside the revenue organization and owns the connection between what customers buy and what they actually get out of Mixpanel. We turn product usage into measurable business outcomes, working across onboarding, adoption, and renewal to make sure customers see the value they signed up for.

About the Role

The right candidate is a relationship-first advisor who connects a customer's Mixpanel investment to real outcomes for a defined book of accounts. You'll own the adoption and value plan for each account end to end: understanding why the customer bought Mixpanel, tracking whether they're getting the ROI they expected, and driving the enablement and product usage that gets them there. You'll build trusted relationships with business and technical stakeholders, partner closely with your Account Executive and renewal counterparts, and bring a growing point of view on how customers should think about AI in their product workflows. This role suits someone who can own a project end to end and is ready to start extending their influence beyond their own accounts to the wider team.

Responsibilities

• Own the value plan for each account in your portfolio, connecting the business problem that led the customer to buy Mixpanel with the outcomes they measure.

• Build relationships with business and technical stakeholders, aligning Mixpanel's capabilities to what customers care about most.

• Run discovery on customer priorities and pain points, and turn what you learn into concrete adoption plans and internal updates.

• Partner with your Account Executive on expansion and your renewal counterpart on renewal execution, bringing the value case and adoption evidence that supports both.

• Lead enablement/best practices sessions on dashboard design, funnel analysis, and retention modeling to grow how deeply and widely a customer uses Mixpanel.

• Monitor usage and health signals and lead business reviews that surface what's working, deepen adoption, and catch risk early.

• Spot underused features and contracted capabilities, and turn them into clear recommendations for the customer.

• Triage product questions and issues, solving what you can and routing the rest to the right team.

• Build a working point of view on a customer's AI maturity, and use Mixpanel's own AI surface to help them build on their product data.

• Coordinate with GTM, Product, and Engineering on escalations, and share what works with the broader Customer Value Architects team.

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

• 4 - 6 years of experience in customer success, consulting, or a related field supporting B2B SaaS accounts, or equivalent experience.

• A track record of managing relationships across a range of stakeholders, from business partners to technical teams.

• The ability to translate technical concepts, like data models and product metrics, into terms that land with non-technical stakeholders.

• Experience turning product usage into a clear story about customer outcomes and ROI.

• Comfort building and running adoption plans that tie daily work to a customer's larger goals.

• Hands-on experience with AI or agentic tooling beyond casual use, such as MCP-based workflows or LLM copilots.

• A collaborative approach to working across account teams and internal partners to move plans forward.

• Good judgment for prioritizing which accounts and actions need attention first.

Bonus Points For

• Background in product analytics, growth, or data-driven product development.

• Experience in a technical advisory or professional services capacity.

• Familiarity with analytics instrumentation, event tracking, or data tooling.

#LI-Remote

Benefits and Perks

• Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental Care

• Mental Wellness Benefit

• Generous Vacation Policy & Additional Company Holidays

• Enhanced Parental Leave

• Volunteer Time Off

• Additional US Benefits: Pre-Tax Benefits including 401(K), Wellness Benefit, Holiday Break

*please note that benefits and perks for contract positions will vary*

Culture Values

• Make Bold Bets: We choose courageous action over comfortable progress.

• Innovate with Insight: We tackle decisions with rigor and judgment - combining data, experience and collective wisdom to drive powerful outcomes.

• One Team: We collaborate across boundaries to achieve far greater impact than any of us could accomplish alone.

• Candor with Connection: We build meaningful relationships that enable honest feedback and direct conversations.

• Champion the Customer: We seek to deeply understand our customers’ needs, ensuring their success is our north star.

• Powerful Simplicity: We find elegant solutions to complex problems, making sophisticated things accessible.

Why choose Mixpanel?

We’re a leader in analytics with over 29,000 customers and $277M invested from prominent investors: like Andreessen-Horowitz, Sequoia, YC, and, most recently, Bain Capital. Mixpanel’s pioneering event-based data analytics platform offers a powerful yet simple solution for companies to understand user behaviors and easily track overarching company success metrics. Our accomplished teams continuously facilitate our expansion by tackling the ever-evolving challenges tied to scaling, reliability, design, and service. Choosing to work at Mixpanel means you’ll be helping the world’s most innovative companies learn from their data so they can make better decisions.

Mixpanel is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. At Mixpanel, we are focused on things that really matter—our people, our customers, our partners—out of a recognition that those relationships are the most valuable assets we have. We actively encourage women, people with disabilities, veterans, underrepresented minorities, and LGBTQ+ people to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance or other similar laws that may be applicable, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We’ve immersed ourselves in our Culture and Values as our guiding principles for the impact we want to have and the future we are building.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/mixpanel-customer-value-architect-iii-1

title: Product Lead - Infrastructure
description:
Supabase (https://jobicy.com/company/supabase) is the open-source Postgres development platform that 10M+ developers and thousands of enterprises depend on every day. Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime and Vector Search all run on one platform: the same compute (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/compute-add-ons), the same disks (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/database-size), the same network and control plane, in every region we operate.

Supabase's hardest problems live in that platform. Millions of databases, growth that compounds every quarter, and a customer base running from a developer on a free project to a regulated enterprise routing traffic through PrivateLink (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/privatelink). Reliability, capacity, cost and the enterprise features that close deals all come back to the same primitives. We're hiring a Product Lead to own them.

About the role

You own the platform primitives every Supabase product runs on: compute, disks, networking, the API gateway, capacity and regions. You own the enterprise surfaces built on top of them too, including read replicas (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/read-replicas), custom domains (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/custom-domains), PrivateLink and Bring Your Own Cloud. You report to the Head of Product and set direction for the whole area alongside the leads for our other product lines. You're the only product person on the platform today, and the team grows under you as the area does.

What you'll be responsible for:

•
You talk to customers across the full spectrum. Developers running a single small project, growing startups whose bill is mostly compute and disk, enterprises walking through a network architecture review, and partners building on top of Supabase.

•
You own the problem statement and requirements behind every platform bet. You define what we're building and why before engineering starts, name the cost, capacity and reliability constraints, and keep that clarity current through execution.

•
You decide what gets built, what gets deferred, and what gets cut. Every quarter you're choosing between enterprise unlocks that open new markets, cost and performance wins for the long tail of projects, and net-new capabilities that change what Supabase can run. The priorities are yours, and so is defending them.

•
You own reliability as a product surface. You set service levels that track what customers experience, hold teams to them, and show customers what it takes to run millions of databases.

•
You define how each launch is measured before it ships. The metric, the threshold and the read afterwards are yours: whether a launch moved enterprise deal velocity, project economics, or platform reliability.

•
You keep engineering, design and leadership aligned. The platform touches every other Supabase product, every region and every customer tier. You write down what's coming, why, and in what order, and you surface dependencies before they become blockers.

You might be a good fit if you:

•
Have 8+ years of product management experience on developer tools, or are an ex-founder who has built in this space. You're technical enough to read an architecture doc and follow a design discussion.

•
Have shipped cloud infrastructure as a product. You've owned at least one of compute, networking, storage, or multi-region and multi-tenant systems at a cloud, infrastructure or PaaS company, as the owner rather than a neighbouring team. You can judge the tradeoffs: instance sizing and capacity, disk and storage economics, scale-to-zero versus always-on, single-tenant versus shared, and the distance between "works in one region" and "works in twenty." Familiarity with how enterprises buy infrastructure (PrivateLink, BYOC, procurement) is a bonus.

•
Have grown with an infrastructure product. You've owned infrastructure small enough to hold in your head, and stayed with it until capacity, regions and cost became the real constraints.

•
Are biased toward speed. You'd rather ship something imperfect and learn from it.

•
Build with what you own. You stand up a read replica, put a custom domain in front of a project, terminate traffic through PrivateLink, deploy onto BYOC. You develop opinions through first-hand use.

•
Use AI to move faster. You lean on AI for the slow parts of the job (research, drafting, synthesising feedback) so you spend more time on judgment calls.

•
Work async by default. We're fully remote. You make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

What We Offer

•
Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•
ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•
Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•
Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•
Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•
Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•
Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•
~400 team members

•
60+ countries

•
20+ languages spoken

•
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

I rely on engineers for technical feasibility, operational risk, and architecture tradeoffs, while maintaining accountability for customer value, prioritization, and launch outcomes. Written decision records and regular review points help surface dependencies early without creating unnecessary meetings. How would you approach bringing an enterprise capability such as BYOC from concept to launch? I would validate the specific enterprise problems, buyer requirements, security and procurement concerns, and willingness to adopt the model. Next, I would define the minimum viable operating model, including deployment boundaries, support expectations, security controls, pricing implications, onboarding, and success criteria. I would pilot with carefully selected design partners, use their feedback to refine the product and documentation, and scale only after the operational and commercial model is proven. Supabase is the open-source Postgres development platform that 10M+ developers and thousands of enterprises depend on every day. Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime and Vector Search all run on one platform: the same compute , the same disks , the same network and control plane, in every region we operate. Supabase’s hardest problems live in that platform. Millions of databases, growth that compounds every quarter, and a customer base running from a developer on a free project to a regulated enterprise routing traffic through PrivateLink . Reliability, capacity, cost and the enterprise features that close deals all come back to the same primitives. We’re hiring a Product Lead to own them. About the role You own the platform primitives every Supabase product runs on: compute, disks, networking, the API gateway, capacity and regions. You own the enterprise surfaces built on top of them too, including read replicas , custom domains , PrivateLink and Bring Your Own Cloud. You report to the Head of Product and set direction for the whole area alongside the leads for our other product lines. You’re the only product person on the platform today, and the team grows under you as the area does. What you’ll be responsible for: You talk to customers across the full spectrum. Developers running a single small project, growing startups whose bill is mostly compute and disk, enterprises walking through a network architecture review, and partners building on top of Supabase. You own the problem statement and requirements behind every platform bet. You define what we’re building and why before engineering starts, name the cost, capacity and reliability constraints, and keep that clarity current through execution. You decide what gets built, what gets deferred, and what gets cut. Every quarter you’re choosing between enterprise unlocks that open new markets, cost and performance wins for the long tail of projects, and net-new capabilities that change what Supabase can run. The priorities are yours, and so is defending them. You own reliability as a product surface. You set service levels that track what customers experience, hold teams to them, and show customers what it takes to run millions of databases. You define how each launch is measured before it ships. The metric, the threshold and the read afterwards are yours: whether a launch moved enterprise deal velocity, project economics, or platform reliability. You keep engineering, design and leadership aligned. The platform touches every other Supabase product, every region and every customer tier. You write down what’s coming, why, and in what order, and you surface dependencies before they become blockers. You might be a good fit if you: Have 8+ years of product management experience on developer tools, or are an ex-founder who has built in this space. You’re technical enough to read an architecture doc and follow a design discussion. Have shipped cloud infrastructure as a product. You’ve owned at least one of compute, networking, storage, or multi-region and multi-tenant systems at a cloud, infrastructure or PaaS company, as the owner rather than a neighbouring team. You can judge the tradeoffs: instance sizing and capacity, disk and storage economics, scale-to-zero versus always-on, single-tenant versus shared, and the distance between “works in one region” and “works in twenty.” Familiarity with how enterprises buy infrastructure (PrivateLink, BYOC, procurement) is a bonus. Have grown with an infrastructure product. You’ve owned infrastructure small enough to hold in your head, and stayed with it until capacity, regions and cost became the real constraints. Are biased toward speed. You’d rather ship something imperfect and learn from it. Build with what you own. You stand up a read replica, put a custom domain in front of a project, terminate traffic through PrivateLink, deploy onto BYOC. You develop opinions through first-hand use. Use AI to move faster. Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.
